title: Does Privacy Regulation Harm Content Providers? A Longitudinal Analysis of the Impact of the GDPR
eligible_reason: The headline design (Table 2: EUWeb x after_gdpr) has a single adoption date (GDPR, wave 26) and is not eligible. But Table 4 reports a Callaway-Sant'Anna estimate (csdid, dripw, notyet, long2) of the effect of EU websites adopting a cookie-consent mechanism, with the cohort variable built from the first wave in which EUWeb*ConsentMechanism == 1 (csgvar): 322 EU websites adopt across 13 waves (22-34) and US websites plus non-adopting EU websites are never treated. Table 5 reports static TWFE regressions of six outcomes on the binary ConsentMechanism indicator with website and wave fixed effects and no controls on the post-GDPR EU sample, where adoption is staggered across waves 26-34. Both satisfy the binary staggered-treatment, unit + time FE, no-controls rules; the TWFE counterpart of Table 4 can be constructed from the same data.
design_notes: Website-by-crawl-wave panel (Main_Table2to5.dta: 21,798 rows, 910 websites, 465 EU, 24 waves numbered 11-34; after_gdpr = 1 from wave 26). Table 1 (Table1_IPLvl.dta): triple interactions EUWeb x after_gdpr x eu_IP for tracking outcomes (single date). Table 2: reghdfe Y (1.EUWeb)#1.after_gdpr, absorb(id_web wave_num) cluster(id_web) for six outcomes, repeated with eu_5euvisitors and a continuous ShareEUVisitors treatment (single date, not eligible). Table 3: EUxPost plus CMxShare NoAdsTrCkxShare CWxShare BEUxEU (multiple treatment regressors, not eligible). Table 4 (lines 117-131): gen eu_postGPDR = EUWeb*ConsentMechanism; egen cs_treatment_mins = csgvar(eu_postGPDR), tvar(wave_num) ivar(id_web); csdid url_gdelt, time(wave_num) gvar(cs_treatment_mins) dripw notyet long2; estat simple. Only url_gdelt is run in the shipped code (global dvs reset to url_gdelt), although the esttab mgroups pattern suggests the published table may have six columns; verify. Table 5 (lines 147-168): preserve; drop if EUWeb==0; drop if after_gdpr==0; bys id_web: egen anycm = sum(ConsentMechanism); reghdfe Y ConsentMechanism if anycm>0, absorb(wave_num id_web) cluster(id_web) for six outcomes. Figure 4: xtdidregress with a single-date treatment (not eligible). ConsentMechanism is not monotone: 58% of EU websites have monotone CM paths; csgvar takes the first treated wave (confirm in Stata).
main_or_robustness: secondary (Tables 4-5 are consent-mechanism analyses; the headline Table 2 is a single-date GDPR DiD)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Table 4: first wave with EUWeb*ConsentMechanism == 1 across 322 EU websites: wave 22 (78), 23 (24), 24 (20), 25 (9), 26 (55), 27 (26), 28 (18), 29 (24), 30 (12), 31 (5), 32 (26), 33 (16), 34 (9); 588 websites (445 US + 143 EU) never treated. Table 5 sample (EU, waves 26-34, anycm>0): 50 already treated at wave 26, 266 switch on at waves 27-34 (8 cohorts).
modern_estimators_named: callaway_santanna (Stata csdid, dripw, notyet control, long2)

specs.outcome: url_gdelt (number of new articles per wave, GDELT)
specs.treatment_var: cs_treatment_mins (cohort variable from csgvar(eu_postGPDR)); eu_postGPDR = EUWeb*ConsentMechanism
specs.treatment_definition: cohort = first crawl wave in which an EU website displays a consent mechanism; 0 for US websites and EU websites that never display one. TWFE counterpart: D = 1(cs_treatment_mins>0 & wave_num>=cs_treatment_mins)
specs.fe: Callaway-Sant'Anna cohort-by-period ATTs (csdid), not-yet-treated plus never-treated controls, doubly-robust IPW without covariates, long2 base period; aggregated with estat simple
specs.sample_condition: full Main_Table2to5.dta sample with non-missing url_gdelt (17,588 rows)
specs.reported_location: Table 4 (coef labelled 'EU Website x Consent Mechanism')
specs.notes: Shipped code runs only url_gdelt; published Table 4 may contain the other five outcomes (esttab mgroups pattern for six columns). ConsentMechanism switches off for some sites after first adoption; protocol: drop post-adoption periods with treatment off when building the TWFE/BJS counterparts.

specs.treatment_definition: 1 if the EU website displays a cookie-consent mechanism in the crawl wave, 0 otherwise (website-level, switches on at website-specific waves; switches off in ~13% of post-adoption site-waves)
specs.time_var: wave_num (crawl wave; waves 26-34 in this sample)
specs.sample_condition: EUWeb==1 & after_gdpr==1 (post-GDPR waves 26-34) & anycm>0 (website has a consent mechanism in at least one post-GDPR wave); 316 websites, 2,838 site-waves (2,247 for url_gdelt and reaction_mean)
specs.notes: 50 websites already have CM at wave 26 (always treated in this sample), 266 switch on at waves 27-34 (8 cohorts); no never-treated units (not-yet-treated comparisons only). Per protocol, drop post-adoption site-waves where ConsentMechanism reverts to 0.

data_files: Replication Files/Dta/Main_Table2to5.dta (1.5 MB; 21,798 website-waves; variables wave_num url_gdelt page_view_per_million page_view_per_user rank reach_per_million reaction_mean after_gdpr id_web eu_5euvisitors EUWeb ShareEUVisitors CMxShare NoAdsTrCkxShare CBxShare CWxShare BEUxEU EUxPost ConsentMechanism)
data_files_note: All analysis files shipped; web-crawl and Alexa/GDELT/Facebook-derived panel at the website-wave level.
software_notes: Stata 17.1 SE (reghdfe, csdid, estout, erepost); Python only for Sankey diagrams.
priority_note: Eligible via Table 4 (CSA) and Table 5 (TWFE); data present; small file. Note these are secondary analyses and the treatment (adopting a consent mechanism) is a website choice, not the GDPR itself.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Verified in Main_Table2to5.dta: 24 waves, GDPR at wave 26, 322 EU adopters over 13 cohorts, 316 websites in the Table 5 sample (50 always treated, 266 switchers), ConsentMechanism non-monotone for 42% of EU sites. The csgvar semantics (first treated wave) should be confirmed when running Stata. Table/column labels inferred from do-file section headers; verify against the article.
